purpose: Balsalazide is used to treat ulcerative colitis, a condition that causes inflammation and sores in your large intestine. It helps reduce symptoms like diarrhea, rectal bleeding, and stomach pain. It is used to bring on remission and help keep your symptoms under control.
how_it_works: Balsalazide travels through your digestive system until it reaches your large intestine, where it is broken down into an active ingredient called mesalamine. Mesalamine works by reducing inflammation directly in the lining of your colon. Think of it as putting out the fire of irritation right where it is happening in your gut.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include headache, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhea, and vomiting. Some people also notice joint pain or a general feeling of not feeling well. These effects are usually mild and often improve as your body adjusts to the medication.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have kidney problems, as this medicine could potentially affect your kidneys over time. Let your doctor know if you are allergic to aspirin or salicylate medications, since balsalazide is related to those drugs. Contact your doctor right away if you develop severe stomach pain, bloody diarrhea, or signs of a serious allergic reaction like rash, swelling, or difficulty breathing.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is three 750 mg capsules taken three times a day with or without food, for up to 8 to 12 weeks. Your doctor may adjust this based on your condition and how you respond to treatment. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes and do not stop without talking to them first.
